## Summary of the last run

The page is a careful development of Giraud's theorem via a site on a generating subcategory. I checked the proofs (topology axioms, representable presheaves are sheaves, coproduct preservation, subobject correspondence, and the main theorem) and the side remarks. The proofs are logically sound: the uses of (G2), (G3), (G4), the regular-epi/kernel-pair facts, and the locally-bijective criterion are all consistent with the cited results. The supplement's statements about the canonical topology and geometric morphisms are standard and correctly hedged as 'known but not included on this site'. I found no genuine logical gap, missing hypothesis, improper link, or false side claim worth reporting; the one candidate I examined (the 'largest topology' phrasing) is in fact a correct characterization of the canonical topology, so I do not report it.
